clue.text: Old entertainer calming a dicky bird

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for unsound or faulty, so the letters of calming a are knocked out of shape

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A performer of yesteryear soothes an unwell bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky' (British slang for faulty) makes MAGICLAN from the letters of 'calming a'. A magic lantern was a Victorian slide projector, which is why it counts as an 'old entertainer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A projector of painted slides was a popular Victorian form of entertainment, now old-fashioned.

clue.text: Place to drop anchor, say — a space taken up

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
room means space

explanation.surface: A harbour for anchoring, for example a spot claimed by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses EGAROOM, read from the bottom of this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring berth is a spot where a vessel may be tied up or anchored.

clue.text: Miller's material extremely low-grade? That's hard to swallow

parts.note: grist is grain to be ground at a mill

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Poor-quality flour from the mill is difficult to accept.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is tough cartilage in meat that is difficult to chew and get down.

clue.text: Dave's mate gets thirty days, having concealed old rifle

parts.note: Chas and Dave were a British cockney pop duo

indicators.note: having concealed means one piece hides another inside it

parts.note: September has thirty days, abbreviated Sept

explanation.surface: Dave's friend is jailed for a month after hiding an antique gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having concealed' puts O inside SEPT. 'old rifle' looks like one unit but 'old' only gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: The chassepot was a French breech-loading rifle of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: A clipped English accent

parts.note: clipped hair has been cut

explanation.surface: A clipped, cut-glass English way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped English accent' reads as a posh voice; the definition is just 'accent', a diacritic mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute is a diacritic accent mark, as on the e in café.

clue.text: Explorer who is standing firm leaves for a smoke

indicators.note: in a down clue standing means upright, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: John Cabot was a Venetian explorer who sailed for England
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An explorer holding his ground goes off to have a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns CABOT into TOBAC. 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun, part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is the dried leaf of a plant that is smoked in pipes and cigarettes.

clue.text: Prince with more cats and dogs?

definitions.meaning: Prince ... III of Monaco, husband of Grace Kelly
raining cats and dogs is heavy downpour, so more of it is wetter weather

explanation.definitionFit: Rainier was the ruling prince of Monaco, and also means wetter, with heavier showers.

clue.text: I got landline working — that means phone may be used

definitions.text: that means phone may be used

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: I have had my home telephone connected, so calls can now be made.
explanation.definitionFit: The steady sound in a handset shows the line is live and a number can be keyed.

clue.text: Island almost won by lucky man before a battle

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as the word itself before trimming
Lucky Jim is Kingsley Amis's comic novel, so the lucky man is Jim

explanation.surface: An island nearly captured by a fortunate fellow ahead of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims WON to WO. 'Island' at the start looks like the definition, but it only supplies I; the definition is 'battle', the 1945 Pacific engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific island gave its name to a famous 1945 conflict between American and Japanese forces.

clue.text: Hesitation before one crucified Italian

parts.note: um is the sound of a speaker hesitating
Brian is crucified at the end of Monty Python's Life of Brian

explanation.surface: Someone pauses before naming an Italian who was executed on a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the central region of Umbria is an Italian person.

clue.text: Fliers approaching? Can air force get squadron leader?

parts.note: nigh means near or approaching
a tin is a can
a gale is a forceful wind, a force of air

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Aircraft drawing near: can the air force recruit a squadron commander?
explanation.walkthrough: 'air force' looks like the RAF but is a strong wind; 'squadron leader' is the first letter of 'squadron'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightingales are songbirds, and birds are creatures that fly.

clue.text: Sheds listed by cartographers

parts.note: a ship that has listed has leant over
OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency

explanation.surface: Garden huts appear on a list drawn up by mapmakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listed' reads as 'recorded' but means tilted; the Ordnance Survey (OS) makes Britain's official maps.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, its roof sloping one way.

clue.text: Attractive but ignoring fine print

indicators.note: ignoring tells us to leave out the letter standing for fine

parts.note: fetching means attractive
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Something appealing that overlooks the small print of a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine print' looks like one phrase, but 'fine' gives F and 'print' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from a metal plate engraved with acid.

clue.text: Hampshire needed part in The Forsyte Saga

indicators.note: part tells us the answer is a portion of the run of letters in Hampshire needed

explanation.surface: The actress Susan Hampshire had to have a role in the television Forsyte Saga.
explanation.walkthrough: Susan Hampshire really did act in the 1967 BBC Forsyte Saga, so the surface is apt. The clue is read as 'part [of] Hampshire needed' giving the character in the saga.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene Forsyte, Soames's unhappy wife, is a central character in Galsworthy's novel sequence.

clue.text: Fat cat or animated dog caught stool pigeon

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in Disney cartoons
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a stool pigeon is an informer, a rat

explanation.surface: A rich man, or a cartoon dog, nabbed a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat cat is slang for a wealthy, powerful person, someone ruling through riches.

clue.text: High Court trial that's appropriate when starting sentence?

parts.note: upper means higher up
a case is a matter tried in court

explanation.surface: A proceeding in the High Court that suits the beginning of a prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' suggests a judge's punishment, but it is a written sentence that begins with a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are the correct choice for the first letter of a written sentence.

clue.text: March about Stoke Poges when king is deposed

indicators.note: about signals the remaining letters are turned around and reordered
a deposed king is removed, so the letter for king leaves

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A procession around a Buckinghamshire village once the monarch has been overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is deposed' takes K out of STOKEPOGES, leaving STOEPOGES, and 'about' rearranges it. Stoke Poges is a village in Buckinghamshire, England, home of Gray's Elegy churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose-step is a stiff-legged military way to parade, a form of marching.

clue.text: Keep watch, say

explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch closely, and also to make a remark.

clue.text: Lime tree not left out for recluse

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order
not tells us to omit the letter standing for left

explanation.surface: A lime tree, minus its leftward branch, stands alone as a hermit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not left' removes L from LIMETREE, leaving IMETREE, and 'out' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious hermit, someone living in solitude.

clue.text: One thing after another for school

definitions.meaning: a series or sequence of events following in order
to teach or coach someone in a skill

explanation.definitionFit: A train is a succession of things, and to train is to school or instruct.

clue.text: Alarm bells when harmful substances are mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned signals a word spoken, so we want something sounding alike

parts.note: toxins are poisons, harmful substances

explanation.surface: Warning sirens go off whenever poisons are named.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is a bell rung as an alarm or warning signal.

clue.text: Call for support when cricketer turns up in a play

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to toy is to play

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: Applause when a batsman makes an appearance in a stage drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the cricketer, since this light reads downwards; 'Call for support' is a cheer, not a phone call. In cricket a 'bat' is a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Attaboy is an American exclamation of encouragement, cheering someone on.

clue.text: Old boy's meeting place that's disgusting

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil; the possessive adds no letter
a scene is a place where something happens or people gather

explanation.surface: A former pupil's reunion venue turns out to be revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscene is offensive to decency, repulsive and lewd.

clue.text: Winger showing remorse when missing header

indicators.note: the header of a word is its first letter, which goes missing

parts.note: regret is remorse

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing shows regret after failing to score with his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' and 'header' paint a football scene, but the winger is a bird with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron-like wading bird, a creature with wings.

clue.text: A thrice-cooked kind of biscuit?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are messed about with, as books are cooked

explanation.surface: A biscuit that has been baked three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges ATHRICE. A rich tea is a plain, sweet British biscuit popular for dunking in tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich tea is a popular variety of plain sweet British biscuit, often dunked.

clue.text: Prior possibly more noble?

definitions.meaning: jokingly the comparative of earl, a nobleman, so more like a peer

explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means previous in time, and as a joke means having more of an aristocrat's qualities.

clue.text: Friendly questioning of speaker's power

definitions.meaning: split into three words it is the speaker asking whether they have the capacity to do something

explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means pleasant and friendly, and split up it asks whether I am capable.

clue.text: Offering no respite, bank admits reduced funds for borrowers

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
money advanced to borrowers has been lent
less means reduced or lower

explanation.surface: A bank that offers less to borrowers gives them no relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun but is the verb 'rely'; 'admits' puts LENTLESS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Relentlessly means without letting up, persistently and unceasingly.
